industrial_frontier.screen.changelog.bod:
# Recast 1.0

- The quest book was rebuilt: twelve epochs instead of twenty-seven chapters, quests laid out on a grid, every chapter open from the start.
- Hand recipes were handed to machines. What used to be assembled on a crafting table is now made by the press, mill, saw, coke oven and blast furnace.
- Output grows with the tier. A better machine yields more product from the same input, so building the next line pays off.
- Five in-house multiblock machines now work: water treatment, decontamination, radiation control, the stage assembly stand and the swarm service station.
- The Create burner no longer needs a trip to the Nether. It takes ordinary fuel.
- Farming is fully integrated: crop breeding, irrigation and machine harvesting.
- The main menu, loading screens and book styling share one look.

A detailed breakdown lives in the pack's version log.

industrial_frontier.screen.guide.body:
# Recast

Recast is a technology-and-city-building pack about chemical chains, connected factories, living settlements and the road from a field expedition to an interplanetary civilization.

## How to play

Once you enter a world, open the FTB Quests engineering handbook. The main route leads through epochs P0–P9; specialist chapters explain machinery, substances, safety, architecture and logistics. JEI tells you the recipe. The handbook tells you why the process exists and where it belongs in your plant.

## One industrial system

Every process has one owner, every substance has one passport, and all progression answers to one value: `industrial_frontier:tech_epoch`. A by-product needs a consumer or a safe disposal route.

## Pace

Recast does not ask for stockpiles of parts merely to consume time. Scale becomes mandatory only after the line is understood and automation is available.

## Safety

Radiation, pressure, chemical hazards and faction operations must warn the player clearly before an irreversible consequence.
